scenarios.name: scripted-fix-with-tests-on-branch
scenarios.rationale: Both create a branch, use --message with both files, and include --test-cmd with --auto-test; B also mentions /undo and git show/diff, so it covers every rubric item, while A reviews with git diff/git log but never mentions undo or /undo, and its retry loop is extra.

scenarios.name: architect-mode-two-models
scenarios.rationale: B uses --architect with --model opus and --editor-model sonnet, passes CONVENTIONS.md with --read, and says the editor applies the proposal automatically unless --no-auto-accept-architect is passed, which covers every rubric item. A has the first two parts right but wrongly says Aider asks for confirmation by default and never mentions --no-auto-accept-architect.

scenarios.name: persistent-config-lint-test-no-coauthor
scenarios.rationale: Both give a correct .aider.conf.yml with model, lint-cmd list entry, test-cmd, auto-test, read, and attribute-co-authored-by: false; B adds auto-lint and extra attribution options but A hedges less on key claims, and both mention .env only for the Anthropic key, so neither covers the 'other API keys belong in .env' note explicitly, with B slightly more complete overall.
